concerns.message: The adjacent-berth rule plus the spur removal leaves a dead zone of the same kind on the EAST side of the real south docks. At (23,27) the coast east of the berth is one row further north: tiles (24..30,26) are land and (24..25,27) are sea (sliceSeaSketch.ts rows 26-27; simulation.test.ts:567 asserts this). A ship on the sweep's own heading 48 (due north, dx=0, so it doesn't slide) in column 25 grounds at y=27*256+80=6992, tile (25,27), in the dock's own row. For x from 6400 to 6479 its hull overlaps (24,27), the tile right beside the berth, yet it rests sqrt(384²+80²)≈392 or more sub-units from the berth centre. That is outside the 384 reach despite a clear run, and (25,27) isn't a neighbour tile. This is the 'aground about 395, just outside 384' symptom the reviewers blocked on, mirrored. The sweep will report (25,27) as a resting place and the rules let the worker hard-code it with a one-line reason ('south coast two tiles east of the berth'), in all four mirrors. The browser test and the corner test (simulation.test.ts:559) sail at headings N-1 and N-2, which slide west into (24,27), and the synthetic island has no coast east of its berth in the dock's row, so nothing else catches it.
concerns.consequence: The worker ships a sweep that passes by listing a resting place about 392 sub-units from the berth, in its own row with a clear run, where holding E does nothing. A reviewer driving due north at Palm Key's south dock slightly east of the berth reproduces the original complaint, and the run is blocked a third time and reworked. The operator must decide first: either accept orthogonal two-tile resting places at about 392 in decisions.md, or change the neighbour test (see simpler_alternative).

concerns.message: Sweep cost: a ring 2-4 tiles wide on a 64-sub-unit grid is about 600 sea starts per dock. With 5-7 headings and 3 speeds over 9 docks (the synthetic island plus 8 real docks) that is roughly 100,000 lanes. Holding E on every step also calls dockInReach, and the oracle runs alongside it. The unit project uses Vitest's default 5 s timeout (vitest.config.ts sets 20 s only for integration, and that file isn't owned).
concerns.consequence: Without early exits (stop on mooring, on resting, or once the ship leaves the 5×5 block after passing) and an explicit per-test timeout argument, the sweep times out or goes over the 30 s budget on the shared machine, and the unit check fails intermittently.

concerns.message: 'The ring 2–4 tiles from the berth centre' doesn't say how distance is measured. As a straight-line distance (512-1024 sub-units), starts at 512-543 fall inside a diagonal neighbour tile and moor on step 0. Measured in whole tiles (Chebyshev), they don't. The oracle's 'only terrain lookups' also leaves open whether the test copies hullPathIsClear or calls it.
concerns.consequence: The worker picks one reading at random and a reviewer may call the other correct. It's a small change, but it can cost a review round.

concerns.message: Moving the writer into build-map.ts leaves stale references: the test title at maps.test.ts:23 ('run `node assets/source/maps/sketch.ts`'), the header comment in sliceSeaSketch.ts (which says Node runs it directly, so it imports nothing) and the README. package.json isn't owned, so the command has to be a flag on map:build (`npm run map:build -- --from-sketch`), not a new script.
concerns.consequence: The docs point at a command that no longer exists, or the worker edits package.json outside its owned paths and the verifier rejects the run.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Keep the plan, but decide "beside the berth" from the hull's footprint, not the tile under the ship's centre. dockInReach and the test's oracle would accept a ship when any tile its 80-sub-unit hull square overlaps is the berth tile or one of its eight neighbours, with the same diagonal-pinch guard, and otherwise fall back to reach plus a clear run. It's a few lines in each place. It closes the east-side band at (25,27) from 392 to 470 sub-units and the similar band at the west docks' (17,19) and (17,23), and it shrinks the exact rest-tile list to only the tiles that really are far from the berth. If the operator prefers the centre-tile rule, the lighter option is one line in decisions.md: two-tile resting places in the berth's own row or column, down to about 392 sub-units, are accepted by design.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Write a 20-line throwaway vitest test on the base commit using defaultSimulationConfig. For each x from 24*256 to 27*256-1 in steps of 16, place a ship at (x, 29*256+128) with heading 48 and speed 0. Sail it with helm(0, 1, INTERACT_BUTTON) for 60 world steps, then record the final tile, speed, dock, and distance to (23,27)'s berth centre. Apply the proposed centre-tile neighbour rule to the resting points. Any ship at rest in (25,27) at about 392-470 without mooring confirms the east-side dead band before a worker starts. In the same file, time one real dock's full ring sweep (about 10,000 lanes) and multiply by 9 to check the 30 s budget.
